title: The Genie part 2
summary: Choose the queen sacrifice that leaves the lone king without a legal move.

nodes.question: Can White sacrifice the queen to force a draw?
nodes.explanation: After the first illustrated ...Qxb1, White has only king and queen against queen, two bishops and a pawn. Qf5 checks while offering the last piece.

nodes.question: Does the same queen sacrifice work with the king on e3?
nodes.explanation: In this separate source variation, ...Bc3+ has driven the white king to e3 before ...Qxb1. The bishop’s new diagonal completes a different stalemate cage.

nodes.question: Why change the sacrifice when the king reaches d2?
nodes.explanation: The second bishop check has placed the king on d2 and the bishop on d4. Qf5 would no longer stalemate White, so the queen must be offered on another square.

branches.title: Offer the queen with a fork
commentary: Begin after the first ...Qxb1 in the seven-piece final phase. The earlier knight sacrifice, promotion and Bb1 offer remain source context.
Qf5+ checks Kh7 and attacks Qb1 along the diagonal, offering White’s only remaining piece.
Qxf5 is actual stalemate. Kd4 is not in check, and the queen on f5 with bishops on b5 and d2 covers all eight neighboring squares.
branches.explanation: Qxf5 is actual stalemate. Kd4 is not in check, and the queen on f5 with bishops on b5 and d2 covers all eight neighboring squares.

branches.title: Repeat the sacrifice in a shifted cage
commentary: Begin from the separately reconstructed seven-piece diagram after ...Bc3+ Ke3 ...Qxb1, not from an invented connection to the first branch.
Qf5+ again checks and forks the black queen, inviting the capture.
Qxf5 is actual stalemate around Ke3. Bc3 covers d4 and d2, Bb5 covers d3 and e2, and the queen covers the remaining flights.
branches.explanation: Qxf5 is actual stalemate around Ke3. Bc3 covers d4 and d2, Bb5 covers d3 and e2, and the queen covers the remaining flights.

branches.title: Change the sacrifice to the h-file
commentary: Begin from the separately reconstructed seven-piece diagram after the second bishop check and ...Qxb1. The saved board shows Kd2, correcting the caption’s Ke2.
Qh8+ offers the queen with check while leaving the white king’s cage untouched.
Kg6 declines that first offer, but puts the king on the queen’s next checking route.
Qh7+ offers the queen again while attacking Qb1 along the diagonal.
Kxh7 is actual stalemate. Qb1 controls c1, d1, e1, c2 and d3; Bb5 controls e2; Bd4 controls c3 and e3. Kd2 itself is not in check.
branches.explanation: Kxh7 is actual stalemate. Qb1 controls c1, d1, e1, c2 and d3; Bb5 controls e2; Bd4 controls c3 and e3. Kd2 itself is not in check.

branches.title: Reuse the earlier sacrifice in the wrong cage
commentary: Compare the source’s warning that the earlier queen sacrifice no longer works with Kd2.
Qf5+ loses the exact drawing resource in this cage.
Qxf5 does not stalemate White: Kc1 remains legal. Black retains an exact win with its queen, bishops and pawn.
branches.explanation: Qxf5 does not stalemate White: Kc1 remains legal. Black retains an exact win with its queen, bishops and pawn.

exercises.prompt: Why does Qf5 fail in this version?
exercises.answer: After ...Qxf5 the square c1 remains available to Kd2. White has a legal king move, so there is no stalemate.

exercises.prompt: Why offer the queen on h7 instead?
exercises.answer: After ...Kxh7 the black queen stays on b1, where it closes c1 and the other first-rank flights. Together with the bishops it stalemates Kd2.

startContext: Begin after the first ...Qxb1 at 84 seconds in a seven-piece final phase. Two additional seven-piece source diagrams show the alternative bishop checks before that capture. The preceding nine-piece setup and eight-piece connecting sequence remain source context and are not certified here. Each reconstructed cage and encoded queen sacrifice is checked exactly.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.

sourceCorrections.claim: The caption names the second king retreat as Ke2.
sourceCorrections.correction: The stable saved diagrams show Kd2 after ...Bd4+. The third stalemate is reconstructed with Kd2; Ke2 is not substituted into the board.
